synopsis: WorkSafe Western Australia is a workplace-safety regulator, distinct from WorkSafe New Zealand, and supplies the Significant Incident Reports cited in the booklet; its material becomes part of the primary legal context when target markets are outside the EU, including Australia [f15673, f15681, f11285]. SIR 226 describes an autonomous haul truck colliding with a manned water cart at night after a route was released in the control system but not marked on the ground, with inadequate change management identified as a contributory cause [f10660, f15684, f10664]. SIR 286 describes operators approaching trucks during recovery without recognizing that they were in exception mode rather than suspended; movement resumed when communications were restored [f10718, f15682]. The reports' web pages carry dates of 11 March 2025 for SIR 226 and 7 March 2025 for SIR 286, but their original issue dates remain uncertain; the research's August 2015 dating of the SIR 226 incident is not stated in the page text [f10666, f10718, f11207, f11208]. WorkSafe's 2025 mobile autonomous mining code warns of additional risks when autonomous and manned operations are integrated and calls for continuing supplier–mine consultation, while the review also cites WorkSafe WA among sources documenting false alarms, rejection, overrides and desensitization [f10720, f10721, f10496].

relations.note: Both describe SIR 286 recovery-mode misunderstanding and movement resuming after communications restoration.
